In this degree, you'll undertake eight foundational science subjects designed to give you a comprehensive foundational science knowledge in biology, chemistry and the natural world. You'll then commence your major studies, building your specialised knowledge of marine biology and climate change, including coral reef and aquatic ecosystems, the impacts of climate change and environmental protection and management. You will also have the opportunity to select elective units from other disciplines, such as policy, law, tourism, and business, and can pursue an on- or off-campus internship for academic credit.

programmes.nameEn: Diploma in Fashion and Sustainability
programmes.descriptionEn: Get the foundations you need for an exciting fashion career and open up a pathway to further study.

detailSections.bodyEn: Get the foundations you need for an exciting fashion career and open up a pathway to further study.
arrow_right_alt How to apply arrow_right_alt Entry pathways arrow_right_alt Eligibility arrow_right_alt Visit our hub for students

This course can be completed in just six months of full-time study or one year part-time. You'll begin by studying the practice of fashion design and design thinking, covering key theories, research techniques, histories and concepts like fashion as art. From there, you'll build competencies in fashion illustration, both by hand and using digital tools like Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop. You'll get hands-on in the studio to learn about patternmaking, construction and the production of garments, then curate your learning journey with your choice of options subjects.

In this degree, you'll complete a number of core business subjects including Business and Social Impact, Marketing and Customer Value and People and Organisations. This will build your vital capabilities and grant you a broad understanding of the way modern organisations work. You'll then commence studies towards your chosen major. Your major choice represents your specialised learning path and will likely influence your future career. You can further tailor your learning through a second major or sub-major or choose to enhance your knowledge by completing elective units from other UTS faculties. Skills you’ll develop Solve business problems using evidence, creativity and critical reasoning. Communicate clearly for different audiences. Work independently and collaboratively to achieve shared goals. Make responsible and inclusive business decisions. Apply technical and professional business skills. Apply knowledge relevant to working with and for Indigenous peoples in professional business contexts.

As a pharmacy student, you’ll combine the study of therapeutics and pharmaceutical sciences with the theory and practice of designing, developing, implementing and evaluating professional pharmacy services. You’ll explore ideas like systems thinking and futures thinking, and experiment with different creative methods. These approaches will help you see problems from fresh perspectives and design solutions that make a real impact. You’ll also develop the skills to be an intrapreneur, someone who drives innovation within an organisation, as well as an entrepreneur or social entrepreneur. programmes.nameEn: Bachelor of Science Master of Teaching in Secondary Education
programmes.descriptionEn: Prepare for a dynamic teaching career with deep disciplinary knowledge and practical experience in science.

detailSections.bodyEn: Prepare for a dynamic teaching career with deep disciplinary knowledge and practical experience in science.
arrow_right_alt How to apply arrow_right_alt Entry pathways arrow_right_alt Eligibility arrow_right_alt Visit our hub for students

Choose a path that allows you to specialise in teaching Biology and Earth and Environmental Science; Chemistry, Physics and Maths; Maths and Physics; or Chemistry and Physics. In the Bachelor of Science, you must complete 96 credit points of disciplinary content subjects comprising 48 credit points of core foundational studies and 48 credit points of more advanced disciplinary content related to the teaching specialisations chosen. In the Master of Teaching in Secondary Education component, you’ll complete 96 credit points comprising 54 credit points of core subjects focused on the foundation education disciplines of learning, motivation, and adolescent psychology; crucial areas including, Indigenous Australian studies, integration of digital technologies in teaching and inclusive education, as well as professional experience, and 42 credit points of teaching methods and electives. You'll need to achieve a credit average after four sessions of full-time study (or part-time equivalent), typically at the end of your second year, to progress into the final years of the program. You’ll also need to complete the NSW Government’s LANTITE Literacy and Numeracy test before progressing to the first Professional Experience supervised teaching placement in Year 3.

Along with establishing a thorough knowledge of economic fundamentals, such as econometrics and behavioural economics, you'll also build core business capabilities, such as strategic decision-making, business statistics, and policy evaluation. Learning from the leaders in social justice, you’ll also become the ethical, sustainable, socially conscious leader of tomorrow. Explore the link between economics and social justice, including the impacts of economic policy on equity, equality and sustainable development, and graduate ready to do good in your chosen career.

programmes.nameEn: Bachelor of Business Bachelor of Laws
programmes.descriptionEn: Combined undergraduate degree integrating business, management and law, developing commercial, legal and professional skills for leadership across industry roles.

detailSections.bodyEn: Combined undergraduate degree integrating business, management and law, developing commercial, legal and professional skills for leadership across industry roles.
arrow_right_alt How to apply arrow_right_alt Entry pathways arrow_right_alt Eligibility arrow_right_alt Visit our hub for students

Flexible and practical, the Bachelor of Business allows you to build essential, job-ready skills with majors in areas like marketing, accounting, human resource management, finance and more. After your first year, you can choose your major, giving you time to consider your options before deciding on your path. In your Bachelor of Law program, you’ll undertake a variety of core studies, developing your knowledge of the Australian legal system, from contracts to the Constitution. You’ll also have the opportunity to enhance your degree by majoring in Legal Futures and Technology.

programmes.nameEn: Master of Business Analytics
programmes.descriptionEn: Study business analytics at UTS and develop expertise in data analytics, visualisation, machine learning and strategic decision-making.

detailSections.bodyEn: Study business analytics at UTS and develop expertise in data analytics, visualisation, machine learning and strategic decision-making.
arrow_right_alt How to apply arrow_right_alt Entry pathways arrow_right_alt Eligibility arrow_right_alt Visit our hub for students

Businesses able to make better decisions using data will be the ones that prosper in global, highly competitive markets awash with information. Professionals who want to succeed in a data-driven world will not only understand the numbers but also be able to communicate insights and prescribe action. These two strands come together in UTS’s new Master of Business Analytics, designed to meet the needs of professionals with either a business or an IT background who are looking for a boundary-crossing degree to take them forward. This course totals 72 credit points. A unique feature of the Business Analytics program is the inclusion of studios, where you'll apply the technical skills you develop onto practical projects.

You will complete 4 core subjects totalling 24 credit points, including the chance to solidify your theoretical learning in your hands-on studio subject, where you’ll identify solutions to real business problems. Graduates of this course who wish to pursue further education can articulate into the UTS Master of Business Analytics. The course is suitable for those from both business snd IT backgrounds who seek to upskill and develop the skills required to meet the growth in emerging careers in business analytics.

programmes.descriptionEn: Advance your study in the disciplinary areas of accounting, finance and economics, management or marketing.

detailSections.bodyEn: Advance your study in the disciplinary areas of accounting, finance and economics, management or marketing.
arrow_right_alt How to apply arrow_right_alt Entry pathways arrow_right_alt Eligibility arrow_right_alt Visit our hub for students

This degree seeks to provide you with the knowledge, competencies and values necessary for a fulfilling and effective career in business. You may undertake one of five streams, including accounting, economics, finance, management or marketing. Each stream is designed to provide you with the necessary knowledge and research skills, leading to a thesis that contributes original insights to your chosen field. This course comprises 48 credit points of study.
